title: US Completes Sixth Night of Strikes on Iran as Tehran Fires Back at Gulf Bases
excerpt: Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz halted again as both sides exchange fire, with Iran targeting U.S. facilities in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan. A child was injured by shrapnel in Qatar.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • The U.S. military completed a sixth consecutive night of strikes on Iranian military targets
  • Iran retaliated with missiles and drones at U.S. bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan; a child was injured by shrapnel in Qatar
  • Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has largely halted again, pushing up global energy prices

The United States completed a sixth consecutive night of strikes on Iranian military facilities on Thursday as the conflict escalated into a cycle of daily attacks and counterattacks, largely halting shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and threatening to pull energy prices higher.

The Strikes

U.S. Central Command said forces including fighter jets, aerial drones, and warships launched precision munitions that hit dozens of Iranian military targets on Qeshm Island and near Bandar Abbas — home to Iran's largest port and key navy and Revolutionary Guards facilities.

"U.S. forces launched precision munitions that hit dozens of Iranian military targets such as coastal surveillance and air defense sites, military logistics infrastructure, and maritime capabilities," CENTCOM said in a statement, adding the strikes were carried out "at President Trump's direction."

Iranian media reported that five bridges were hit in the latest round, along with the train station in coastal Bandar Khamir and Iranshahr Airport in southeastern Iran. Seven people were killed in U.S. attacks on bridges in Bandar Khamir, state news agency IRNA reported.

Iran Fires Back

Iran responded with missiles and drones targeting U.S. military bases across the Gulf region. In the early hours of Friday, Iran's military said it had attacked U.S. facilities in Bahrain and Kuwait. Several explosion-like sounds were heard in the Qatari capital Doha, and the Ministry of the Interior said a child was injured by shrapnel.

Kuwait said its armed forces intercepted four missiles and 21 drones from Iran on Wednesday in an attack that caused material damage but no injuries. The conflict has killed thousands and displaced millions, mainly in Iran and Lebanon.

Hormuz Blocked Again

The escalation has once again largely halted traffic through the Strait of Hormuz, the world's most important shipping route for oil and gas. Tehran resumed its blockade of the strait, and Washington again blockaded Iranian ports from Wednesday.

The renewed fighting has cast doubt on an interim U.S.-Iran agreement signed last month that was intended to reopen the strait and provide a framework for ending the war through an additional 60 days of negotiations. U.S. stock markets fell sharply after the latest strikes, with the Nasdaq slumping 1.7%.

Why It Matters for the Diaspora

The Strait of Hormuz carries roughly one-fifth of the world's oil shipments. Any sustained disruption could spike fuel costs and inflation globally, directly affecting NRI households and Indian-American consumers already navigating high living costs. India, which imports over 80% of its crude oil, is particularly exposed — with Gulf disruptions historically triggering price shocks that ripple through the Indian economy.
